## Project Overview

The goal of this project is to examine how historical patterns of racial segregation in Charlotte-Mecklenburg Schools (CMS) help contextualize present-day racial inequalities in school discipline and law-enforcement contact. Drawing on historical research surrounding school desegregation efforts throughout Mecklenburg County, I first take a look at how the end of race-based school assignment and busing have shaped educational inequalities. I then pull from more recent school-level data to explore what these patterns look like now. I look at the racial composition of schools and the geographic dispersal of said schools, disciplinary outcomes, and law-enforcement referrals. My hope is that these connections are able to create a framework that highlights how educational inequalities put certain subgroups of students at a higher risk for interacting with the criminal legal system.
